text:
maria: quick follow-up on the Service Auth RFC — we need a concrete plan for cross-project/service token handshakes. lots of product asks around: short-lived tokens, resource-scoped api-keys, and a path to migrate long-lived keys without breaking customers. cc @jordan @kevin

jordan: +1. can we outline the tradeoffs in this thread? thinking in terms of three options: 1) keep long-lived project-scoped API keys + enhanced RBAC, 2) introduce a token-broker for short-lived tokens (control-plane minting), 3) mTLS + cert rotation for dedicated infra.

sam_k: option 2 seems best for security, but adds control-plane load. we should quantify token mint rates. also need to decide if tokens are audience-bound (resource-level) or just project-scoped.

kevin: for high-throughput internal calls (e.g., realtime cache reads) short-lived tokens add perf overhead. maybe allow a "service credential" mode where dedicated pools can use a pinned cert. but public APIs should migrate to short-lived tokens.

maria: proposed ruleset: - user-facing API keys stay project-scoped and long-lived but can be limited by resource tag + rate policy - service-to-service should default to short-lived bearer tokens minted by a broker with optional audience claim - provide an escape hatch: machine/service account with pinned certs (mTLS) for low-latency paths

tia: sounds reasonable. how do we map this to RBAC? do we keep current role model (org/project -> roles) or move to resource-ACLs?

jordan: keep roles as primary, but support resource-level grants for sensitive objects. RBAC evaluation order: explicit resource grant -> project role -> org role. this helps least privilege without exploding policy count.

sam_k: migration question: customers currently have lots of long-lived API keys embedded in services. what's our migration UX? immediate rotation breaks them.

maria: plan: 1) add soft enforcement flags (console + API) that allow a project to opt into "short-lived-only" mode 2) default new projects to short-lived tokens 3) build compatibility broker endpoint that accepts old keys and returns a short-lived token for 30d transition window 4) telemetry to find top callers so we can reach out

kevin: broker idea is good. implementation sketch: broker validates long-lived key -> issues JWT with claims {sub, aud, exp, scopes} signed by control-plane KMS. sample exchange:```bash
curl -X POST https://broker.redwood.internal/v1/token -H "x-api-key: <old-key>" -d '{"aud":"svc:cache","ttl":300}'
# returns {"access_token":"ey...","expires_in":300}
```

add rate-limit + IAM check on broker.

maria: security notes: - tokens MUST be audience-bound + have short TTL - revoke list for broker-issued tokens (use revocation index + token ids) - audit logs emitted on mint and revoke - rotate broker signing keys via KMS with overlap window

tia: console/ops side: we need UI to show which keys are eligible for migration and a per-key last-used timestamp. also an API to bulk migrate keys to broker tokens (admin-only).

sam_k: ok. one more edge: cross-tenant calls (service in org A calling resource in org B). what's the auth flow?

jordan: two patterns: 1) delegate via a persona in target org (service account in B granted role, A requests token for that persona via broker), or 2) federation: trust tokens signed by A if A is on allowlist (requires org-to-org trust config). prefer 1 for explicit grants.

kevin: federation adds complexity and risk. if we do it, require mTLS or signed OIDC metadata exchange + short TTL. probably postpone federation until we have strong telemetry on need.

maria: agreed. put federation as v2. action items: - jordan: write a short design doc for broker API + rate limits (ETA 3d) - kevin: prototype broker signing flow + KMS rotation (ETA 1w) - sam_k: list product customers with >10k calls/day using long-lived keys (help from billing) - tia: console mockups for migration UI (ETA 1w)

deploy-bot: deploy status: env=staging, service=auth-broker, sha=ab12cd3, status=success :rocket:

sam_k: one more nit: logs must strip full token values; only log token ids or truncated values. we should add obvious helpers in SDKs.

maria: yes. redact in logs + SDK helper to exchange long-lived key for token and handle refresh. we'll add a new endpoint in SDK: `auth.exchangeLegacyKey()`

jordan: also document failure modes: broker unavailability fallback -> allow direct legacy key until scheduled cutoff, and alert on usage spike.

kevin: and for Dedicated/Private customers we should provide an on-prem broker binary (no control-plane calls) that uses local KMS/HSM. note: that needs separate packaging and support runway.

maria: good call. I'll add a section for Private customers in the doc. ok team — thanks. i'll consolidate notes into PR with proposed timeline and send link here when ready. :thumbsup:
